A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCALE optimizer study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and experimental and proof appendices are readable and matchable despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v2 reports original normalization and momentum experiments, SCALE pretraining results on C4, and RoBERTa fine-tuning results on GLUE, including in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds an embedding-layer momentum ablation, further gradient-variance analyses, and a 100B-token LLaMA 7B training run.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains column-wise normalization and first-order momentum restricted to the last layer. Adam treatment of vector parameters was already documented in v2. The additional momentum variant is an ablation, not a revision of SCALE.

E1.justification: C4 language-model pretraining and the same six GLUE fine-tuning tasks remain the evaluated coverage. The additions vary model configurations, tokenization, and training budgets within these retained tasks; they introduce no new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: The external optimizer baseline sets remain unchanged. However, v3 Appendix E, Table 8 adds a directly evaluated first-plus-last-layer momentum variant as a comparator to SCALE and column-normalized SGD without momentum.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds a 100B-token 7B run with batch size 1024 and learning rate sqrt(2) times 1e-4, versus 512 and 1e-4 in the retained 19.7B-token comparison. Gemma-2B's reported budget changes from 40B to 32B tokens. New variance analyses also introduce LLaMA 350M and GPT-125M configurations, the latter explicitly using the GPT-2 tokenizer.

E4.justification: v3 adds first-layer momentum ablations across three model sizes, variance analyses testing model-size and architecture/tokenizer dependence, and a 100B-token 7B stability study. These substantially extend evidence for selective momentum and training stability beyond v2's retained normalization, learning-rate, and overtraining analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and both retain the single-experiment notice for the 19.7B-token 7B comparison. Additional gradient-variance plots extend an existing analysis rather than change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Main Tables 5–6 remain unchanged. v3 adds final perplexity 9.32 for the separate 100B-token run, first-plus-last-layer momentum perplexities 30.35/22.26/16.14, and additional variance curves. Gemma-2B results change from APOLLO/SCALE 11.90/11.80 at 40B tokens to 12.05/11.96 at 32B tokens; these are replaced results under different budgets, not same-setting deterioration.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly declines to present a SCALE convergence proof. v3 adds Theorem 3.1, matrix-norm smoothness and column-wise variance assumptions, and Appendix O's convergence derivation. Appendix N also substantively revises Theorem 2.1's proof through shared Lyapunov coefficients and changed step-size restrictions, while retaining its stated final bound.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain the minimalist two-component optimizer, Adam-level pretraining performance using 35–45% of its memory, and the reported 7B advantage over APOLLO and Muon. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the modest gains from embedding-layer momentum as supporting last-layer-only momentum and the 100B-token trajectory as evidence of stability. Its conclusion explicitly limits evaluation to 7B parameters and 100B tokens. The token-frequency explanation for column normalization already appeared in v2's appendix.

D1.justification: Appendix G documents the new run's two eight-H200 nodes, distributed data parallelism, batch size, and learning-rate scaling; Appendix J identifies the GPT-2 tokenizer. The existing experimental recipe, tuning information, vector-parameter treatment, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Riabinin et al.'s Gluon work and bases its SCALE convergence connection on that framework instead of the earlier discussion of adopting Pethick et al.'s analysis. The broader related-work positioning remains stable; SWAN's publication update does not introduce a new comparator.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, prose and front matter receive limited editing, and acknowledgments, an impact statement, and additional appendix headings are introduced. Existing sections and most explanatory passages retain their narrative order and wording; much of the expansion is new scientific content.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from predominantly single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout, extensively resizing and relocating tables and figures and stacking previously horizontal panels. v3 also adds Table 8 and Figures 5–7; retained appendix figures are renumbered and relocated.

improvement.justification: The 100B-token run and targeted ablations strengthen empirical support, and the evaluation limits are clearer. However, the newly claimed convergence guarantee has unresolved internal defects: Theorem 3.1 specifies step size a_l/sqrt(T), while Appendix O substitutes a_l*T^(-3/4), and its final noise-decay factor does not follow from the preceding bound. These empirical gains coexist with a newly unsupported theoretical claim, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
